articles.title: Open Source: The Next Generation
articles.description: COSCon'26 — the 11th China Open Source Conference — announces its theme, and opens its call for co-produced events, sponsors, and volunteers.
articles.content:
# Open Source: The Next Generation

**COSCon'26 — the 11th China Open Source Conference — announces its theme, and opens its call for co-produced events, sponsors, and volunteers.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Dates** | November 14–15, 2026 |
| **Venue** | Yungu Center, Hangzhou, China |
| **Organizers** | KaiSource and Datawhale |
| **Theme** | Open Source: The Next Generation |
| **Scale** | 1,000–1,200 attendees, a main forum, and 12 tracks |
| **Format** | Keynotes, thematic forums, workshops and hands-on labs, hackathons, BoFs, community meetups, and an open source bazaar |
| **Proposals in English** | Welcome. Co-production proposals close September 30, 2026 — but see the note for international speakers below |
| **On-site language** | Mostly Mandarin, some tracks in English, AI-assisted live translation; no simultaneous interpretation |
| **Contact** | [board@kaiyuanshe.org](mailto:board@kaiyuanshe.org) |

Every generation of open source people paves the way for the next.

From a single line of code to a project. From a project to a community, and from a community to a way of working together. From a technical ideal to the infrastructure an entire industry runs on. Open source is no longer an option in the software world — it is the default path of innovation in the digital age.

This year COSCon reaches its **eleventh edition**, co-hosted by KaiSource and Datawhale, and comes to Hangzhou for the first time. Eleven years is both the consolidation of one phase and the start of another. Standing at that hinge, we are announcing the theme of COSCon'26:

## Open Source: The Next Generation

This is not a slogan. It is a question we want to ask together, and we think it is the right moment to ask it. As technical paradigms turn over faster, as AI reshapes how things get made, as global collaboration enters a new phase — what will the next era of open source look like? Who defines it? Who takes part? Who benefits?

Our answer: **the next generation of open source is made of next-generation technology, next-generation talent, next-generation communities, and next-generation business.**

## "Next generation" is not just the people who come after us

"Next generation" is not simply the passage of time, nor a replacement of what came before. It means open source is entering a new life cycle: the stack is being rewritten, contributors are turning over, governance is evolving, business models are being rebuilt.

More importantly, it implies agency. Not waiting for the future to arrive — using open source to open it.

COSCon'26 is therefore built around four sub-themes. They are not four islands; they are four gears that mesh, and together they drive the ecosystem forward.

### 1. Next-generation technology: let innovation happen in the open

The next generation of open source technology is becoming the foundation of the current wave of change: large models and agents, cloud native, databases, operating systems, programming languages, RISC-V and open silicon, edge computing, open data, open standards, open source security, and the software supply chain. Every one of these is moving fast. AI makes code generation more efficient — and makes governance, license compliance, and supply chain security far more consequential.

Next-generation open source technology is not only about whether something *works*. It is about whether it is **open, trustworthy, sustainable, and genuinely buildable by many hands**. It has to solve the infrastructure problems of the coming decade, and it has to let more developers, companies, and organizations keep innovating on open shoulders.

**On stage at COSCon'26 we want:** the projects, standards, tools, and practices that are actually defining the next stack — including the unglamorous ones. Post-mortems and hard-won lessons are as welcome as launches.

### 2. Next-generation talent: from user, to contributor, to leader

The future of open source is, in the end, a question about people.

The next generation of open source talent might be a student landing a first pull request. A community mentor. A developer growing from user to maintainer. A university teacher bringing open source into the classroom. An engineer or manager pushing open collaboration from inside a company.

Growing open source talent is not only about writing code. It is collaboration, communication, governance, compliance awareness, project operations, and cross-cultural fluency. Open source in higher education, mentorship programs, internships, hackathons, contributor certification, participation by women and under-represented groups, developer relations — these apparently scattered practices are together forming a path for the next generation.

**On stage at COSCon'26 we want:** programs with evidence behind them. What retained contributors, what quietly failed, and what you would do differently. We want COSCon to be a place where newcomers find a door, contributors are seen, maintainers get support, and the next generation of open source leaders meet each other.

### 3. Next-generation communities: healthier, more open, more sustainable

Community is the heart of open source.

The next generation of communities faces harder problems. How does governance become more transparent? How does contributor experience become genuinely welcoming? How does a code of conduct actually get enforced rather than published? How does collaboration work across languages, time zones, and cultures? How do we secure the community, the supply chain, and the long-term funding that keeps both alive?

At the same time, communities are moving into wider territory: globalization and localization in parallel; foundations, companies, universities, and public institutions all participating; cross-community collaboration becoming routine. A healthy open source community does not only produce code — it builds trust, transfers knowledge, and creates belonging.

The next generation of communities will not be measured by size, but by health; not by how lively they look, but by how long they last.

**On stage at COSCon'26 we want:** open source people from different communities, regions, and backgrounds, talking about governance, contributor experience, inclusion, and what it takes to still be here in ten years.

### 4. Next-generation business: AI is rewriting the organization, and open source with it

Conversations about open source business usually land on open core, subscriptions, hosting, and support. That experience still matters — but it answers the *previous* generation's question: how does software get produced, distributed, and charged for. The real disruption from AI is not one more technology cycle. It is a change in **how organizations are put together**. When the organization changes, the business form changes with it — and open source business gets redefined.

AI is shifting the unit of production from "a department in a company" to a task network of **people + agents + community + platform**. One developer can direct several agents across coding, testing, documentation, and operations. A small team, using open models, open toolchains, and a global community, can ship what used to require a large company. Companies can be smaller and networks larger; less hiring, more collaboration. The way open source communities have always organized — asynchronous, modular, composable, held together by reputation and licenses — is becoming a leading prototype for the AI-native organization.

When organizations move from hierarchies to networks, the commercial logic moves too: from selling software to selling outcomes, from closed products to open ecosystems, from headcount to network effects, from one-time delivery to continuous operation. Open source stops being only a license and a repository. It can become the **trust layer, the collaboration layer, and the distribution layer** of a new kind of business. The corporate OSPO stops being a compliance desk and becomes the hub of open ecosystem strategy and AI governance.

And then value distribution becomes the open question. When models, data, agents, compute, and community contributions all create value together — how do you measure it, split it, govern it? Licenses, open weights, data agreements, AI compliance, contributor incentives: all of them need new answers.

Next-generation open source business is not the old model with an AI prefix. It is a fresh answer to an old question: when AI changes the organization, how is value created, captured, and shared?

**On stage at COSCon'26 we want:** these arguments had in public. Nobody has settled answers — which is exactly why it is worth doing together.

## Why now

Because AI is accelerating everything, and reorganizing everything.

Because the next generation of developers is growing up, the next generation of communities is forming, and the next generation of business models is being tried right now.

Because "next generation" is not a distant future. It is a choice being made today.

From the first edition to the eleventh, COSCon has followed Chinese open source from its first steps to a working ecosystem. The eleventh is the completion of one chapter and the opening of another.

## Take part

The next generation of open source is not the work of a few. We are opening three doors, and we mean all of them to be walkable from outside China as well as inside it.

### 🎤 Co-produce an event

COSCon'26 is co-produced with the communities that show up. Whether you come from a project, a university lab, a foundation, or a startup, you can apply to run your own event inside the conference — and it does not have to be a talk track. Pick the format that fits what you actually want to happen in the room:

- **Thematic forum** — a half- or full-day track on one subject
- **Workshop / hands-on lab** — people leave having built something
- **Hackathon**
- **BoF (Birds of a Feather)** — an open, unstructured session for one topic
- **Community meetup** — bring your community together in person
- **Something else** — tell us what you have in mind

Propose anything under the four sub-themes — or any direction you believe belongs in a conversation about the next generation of open source. **We provide the venue, promotion, and operational support; you bring the content and the people.** The form and the conference program both work in English as well as Chinese.

- **Submit:** [Co-Production Event Application Form](https://kaiyuanshe.feishu.cn/share/base/form/shrcnNtuxyZnwLDL2Beh4yP1P9b) — bilingual, English and Chinese
- **Deadline:** September 30, 2026
- Can't reach the form from where you are? Email us instead: [board@kaiyuanshe.org](mailto:board@kaiyuanshe.org)

> **Speaking from outside China? The September 30 deadline is not your deadline.** That date is for co-production proposals. If you want to speak at COSCon'26 and you are traveling in, write to [board@kaiyuanshe.org](mailto:board@kaiyuanshe.org) and we will work out your participation one to one, on a timeline that fits yours. We would much rather find a place for you on the program than watch you miss a form deadline.

### 🤝 Sponsor

If your organization wants to be part of this ecosystem in a substantial way, COSCon'26 welcomes sponsors and partners. You will meet core developers, community leaders, technical experts, university talent, and industry partners — a place to show your engineering, your open source practice, and your view of where the ecosystem is going, and to find both collaborators and people to hire.

Whether you are building brand presence, looking for projects, connecting with a developer community, or pushing industry-wide collaboration, we would like to hear from you.

- **Contact:** [board@kaiyuanshe.org](mailto:board@kaiyuanshe.org)

### 🙋 Volunteer

At every COSCon there is a group of people in vests and lanyards moving between the halls and the back rooms. They are the first to say "welcome" at the registration desk, the ones fixing a microphone and a projector in the gap between two talks, and the last ones to turn off the lights.

Volunteer recruitment for COSCon'26 is open. Student, developer, designer, community organizer — if you are willing to give a day or two to turn a conference from a plan into a real room full of people, we want you. You will work directly alongside speakers, maintainers, and sponsors, and you will be the most concrete possible footnote to "the next generation."

- **Sign up:** [Volunteer form](https://kaiyuanshe.feishu.cn/share/base/form/shrcnkHNwqkZzzmIfa7HbeL7wtg)
- **Deadline:** October 15, 2026
- Every volunteer receives conference swag and a certificate of participation.

**One thing to know:** the volunteer crew works in Chinese. Briefings, the group chats, and coordination on the day all run in Mandarin, so you will need to be comfortable working in it. If you are traveling in from abroad and still want to help, write to us at [board@kaiyuanshe.org](mailto:board@kaiyuanshe.org) — there may be another way in.

You don't have to write code to build open source. Come, and be the person who makes it happen.

## Coming to Hangzhou from abroad

**Visas.** As of February 2026, China's unilateral visa-free policy covers 50 countries — most of Europe, plus Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Brazil, and others, with the UK and Canada added in February 2026 — and currently runs through December 31, 2026, which covers the conference. If you hold one of those passports, you can enter for up to 30 days without a visa.

**US passport holders are not on that list and still need a visa for an ordinary round trip.** There is one way around it: China's 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit, which does include US nationals. Despite the name it does not require a layover somewhere else first — you can fly direct into Hangzhou, which is an eligible port. What it requires is that you leave China **to a third country or region**, not back where you started.

- ✅ New York → Hangzhou → Tokyo → New York — works
- ❌ New York → Hangzhou → New York — does not; same country at both ends
- ✅ Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan count as third regions for this purpose

So: if you want a simple round trip, get a visa. If you are willing to fly home via Tokyo, Seoul, or Hong Kong, you can skip it. Check the [National Immigration Administration](https://en.nia.gov.cn/n147418/n147463/c183412/content.html) for the rules in force before you book — these lists change.

**Invitation letters.** We issue letters of invitation for visa applications, including for US applicants. Email [board@kaiyuanshe.org](mailto:board@kaiyuanshe.org) as early as you can. Visas are the single most common reason international speakers end up not coming, and processing takes time.

**Come a day early.** We are putting together a program around the conference specifically for people traveling in from abroad — introductions, visits, and unhurried time with the local open source and AI community that two days of talks don't leave room for. Tell us you're coming at [board@kaiyuanshe.org](mailto:board@kaiyuanshe.org) and we will build you into it.

**Language.** We accept session and co-production proposals in English. There is no separate English-language track: each track's working language is decided by the people producing it, and some will run in English. There is no simultaneous interpretation on site, but AI-assisted live translation will be available.

**Getting there.** Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport (HGH) has direct international service. Hangzhou is also about an hour from Shanghai by high-speed rail, so Shanghai's airports are a practical alternative.

## What COSCon looks like

**COSCon'25**, the tenth edition, ran in Beijing under the theme "Open Source, Open Intelligence." It drew **1,500+ people on site** over two days and **86,946 online views** — an all-time high. Twenty-one communities co-created **24 tracks and co-located events**; 54 community and media partners took part, 32 of them exhibiting at the Bazaar; and 230 volunteer applications became a crew of 85.

Guests from **OSI, OpenChain, Open Invention Network, OpenUK, FOSDEM, and United Nations University** attended in person — the most international edition so far.

Across eleven editions the keynote track has run **190 sessions with 136 different speakers**. Two sitting GitHub CEOs have taken part — Nat Friedman in 2018 and Thomas Dohmke in 2019 and 2022 — alongside keynote guests from the Apache Software Foundation, the GNOME Foundation, the Linux Foundation, LF AI & Data, Hyperledger, Ethereum, and Microsoft's Open Source Programs Office. *Titles are as of the year attended; this is a record of who has come, not a lineup for this year.*

KaiSource also travels: in 2025 it took part in the Open Source Congress, CommunityOverCode Asia, GitHub Universe, FOSDEM, State of Open Con, the FOSSASIA Summit, EDCon, GOSIM, and COSCUP. If you have met us at one of those, COSCon is the room where we can return the favor.

## About KaiSource (KAIYUANSHE)

KaiSource (开源社, KAIYUANSHE) is a **volunteer-run, vendor-neutral, non-profit** open source community founded in **2014**, run on the principles of *contribution, consensus, and co-governance*. Our mission spans open source governance, global engagement, community development, and project incubation — rooted in China, contributing worldwide.

KaiSource is the **first member in China of the [Open Source Initiative](https://opensource.org/) (OSI)**, and works closely with open source communities, universities, companies, and public institutions. It was named Open Source Community of the Year on China's 2024 Open Source Innovation List, selected jointly by the China Association for Science and Technology, the China Computer Federation, the China Institute of Communications, and the Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences.

KaiSource has hosted the China Open Source Conference (COSCon) every year since 2016, publishes the [China Open Source Annual Report](https://kaiyuanshe.github.io/2025-China-Open-Source-Report/en/), and co-founded the China Open Source Pioneer List and the China Open Source Code Power List. Over more than a decade it has connected tens of thousands of open source practitioners, over a thousand community members and volunteers, several hundred speakers from China and abroad, and several hundred sponsor, media, and community partners.

---

The next line of code. The next community. The next business model. The next era.

**The next generation of open source is not waiting to be defined by someone else. We write it together.**

COSCon'26 — we hope to open it with you.

*What does "the next generation of open source" mean to you? Tell us at [board@kaiyuanshe.org](mailto:board@kaiyuanshe.org).*

articles.content:
# KaiYuanShe Board Newsletter, Issue 1: June 2026

Dear KaiYuanShe community,

Starting with this issue, the Board will publish a monthly newsletter to share what the community is doing, where we are going, and how people can take part.

This first issue was coordinated by 2026 Chair Richard Lin, but it is not a personal column. Future issues will include contributions from board members, working groups, and community members. We hope this newsletter helps us communicate more clearly and practice contribution, consensus, and co-governance together.

## COSCon 2026 Comes to Hangzhou, November 14-15

The 11th China Open Source Conference will take place at Hangzhou Cloud Valley Center on **November 14-15, 2026**. This is the first COSCon in Hangzhou since the conference began in 2015.

The Call for Tracks will open soon. The program will combine proposals from partner communities with key tracks produced by KaiYuanShe. Sponsorship and collaboration discussions are also open. Contact `board@kaiyuanshe.org`.

## Events in June

- **June 22-23, AWS Summit Shanghai:** KaiYuanShe will host a community booth at the Shanghai World Expo Exhibition and Convention Center. To volunteer, contact Li Mingkang at `slibre@kaiyuanshe.org`.
- **June 22-26, UN Open Source Week in New York:** Liao Jingyi (Lisa), lead of the OpenGood team, will represent the group and discuss open source in sustainable development. Contact `liaojingyi-lisa@outlook.com`.
- **June 25, Advisory Committee meeting in Beijing:** Chen Yang (Emily) will host a closed discussion on GitHub, AI, embodied intelligence, open collaboration, and industry ecosystems at RoboChallenge.
- **June 28, AWS Community Day in Hangzhou:** KaiYuanShe Chair Richard Lin will give the keynote *Signal over Noise: When Data Becomes the New Gold Mine, the Next Arena for AI and Open Source*.

## Recent Community Work

### Open Source Developers in the AI Era

Xu Yin (Ian), KaiYuanShe board member and OpenBuild founder, hosted an online panel titled **If Code Is No Longer the Moat, What Is?** Guests included Chen Zili (tison), Richard Lin, Cui Jiaxi (Panda), and Zhuang Biaowei.

[Watch or read the event review](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s?__biz=MzA4NTM4NDc4NQ==&mid=2247545687&idx=1&sn=b3b145b8bc27f07d4271e455bf0934f0&scene=21#wechat_redirect).

### Open Token and the Paris Initiative

Chen Yang (Emily) moderated a discussion on **Open Token and Digital Public Good** at the GOSIM Paris AI Vision Forum and helped launch the Paris Initiative.

The initiative calls for infrastructure suited to agentic AI, broader access to AI compute and tokens, an agent ecosystem that benefits everyone, and global cooperation among companies, universities, individuals, and foundations. The working group includes participants from the Rust Foundation, MiniMax, Zhipu AI, CSDN, the Institute of Software at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and KaiYuanShe.

- Paris Initiative: https://paris2026.visionforum.ai/initiative/
- Join through GitHub: https://github.com/aivisionforum/paris-2026-initiative/issues/new?template=sign.yml

### KaiYuanShe Joins OIN 2.0

KaiYuanShe has joined Open Invention Network 2.0. OIN is a global defensive patent cross-license network whose members include IBM, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alibaba. This step reflects KaiYuanShe's commitment to software freedom and shared work to reduce patent risk.

## Connecting the Global Chinese-Speaking Open Source Community

More than 20 KaiYuanShe members now work on global collaboration across cities and countries in Asia, Europe, and North America. The community aims to become a two-way bridge between the Chinese-speaking open source world and the wider global ecosystem.

This year's work includes the English edition of the *China Open Source Annual Report 2025*, an English blue paper on China's open source AI ecosystem with Datawhale, international interviews at CommunityOverCode Asia, Linux Foundation events in Shanghai, and international guest programs for COSCon in November.

To join this work, contact Richard Lin at `richard@kaiyuanshe.org`. You can also take part in the public discussion about KaiYuanShe's English brand name at https://github.com/orgs/kaiyuanshe/discussions/13.

## Formal Member Information Update

As of June 16, 78 of 122 formal members had completed the current information update. Formal membership includes voting, election, proposal, and decision-making rights, along with a responsibility to remain involved in community work.

Following notice and the established governance process, members who cannot be reached or are no longer active may move to honorary retired status. This recognizes their past work while keeping governance roles connected to current participation. Anyone who returns to regular contribution is welcome to rejoin the formal member group.

## Volunteer of the Month

**Qi Zihan** joined KaiYuanShe six months ago and has already contributed to COSCon'25 and the Advisory Committee Service Team. As a project manager, she coordinates advisors, board members, and working-group contributors. Her organization and communication have helped the team work more effectively.

## Closing

This is our first monthly Board newsletter, and we will improve its format and focus over time. Most importantly, the Board should continue getting closer to the community.

Send feedback or nominations for contributors who deserve wider recognition to `board@kaiyuanshe.org`.

articles.title: COSCon'25 Wraps Up in Beijing: Ten Years of Open Source Collaboration
articles.description: COSCon'25 marked the tenth China Open Source Conference with 49 booths, more than 200 sessions, 24 themed forums, and a community built across technology, public good, education, and global collaboration.
articles.content:
# COSCon'25 Wraps Up in Beijing

The tenth China Open Source Conference, COSCon'25, concluded successfully in Beijing. Under the theme **Open Source, Open Intelligence**, the event brought together global ideas and practical work from China's open source ecosystem.

This milestone edition featured **49 community and partner booths**, **more than 200 sessions**, and **24 themed forums**. Developers, maintainers, researchers, companies, universities, foundations, students, and volunteers met to share technology, governance experience, and plans for the future.

## AI and Open Source

AI ran through the entire program. The Data for AI Forum covered vector search, document parsing, data lakes, privacy, and compute engines. The Embodied AI Forum connected hardware, algorithms, data platforms, navigation, and real-world applications. A research and industry forum brought together experts from universities, research institutes, and open source companies to discuss how new ideas move from research into practical use.

## Technology in Practice

The program included forums on cloud native systems, open source operating systems and software supply chains, open hardware, RISC-V, automotive software, and Web3.

Speakers discussed practical topics such as Serverless cost control, AI-ready gateways, storage performance, cluster scheduling, software supply-chain security, chip design and verification, autonomous driving, vehicle toolchains, decentralized payments, and open hardware development.

## Communities Meeting in Person

Several established communities held co-located events. Rust Forward 2025 featured work from industry engineers, researchers, and students. Pulsar Developer Day focused on reliable messaging systems and architecture at scale. The OpenChain Forum brought together international organizations, lawyers, and engineers to discuss open source compliance and supply-chain risk.

The event also celebrated the first anniversary of the Whale Intelligence community, with experts from research institutes, AI projects, technology companies, and security organizations.

## Supporting the Next Generation

Twelve young developers, most of them secondary-school students, spoke at the Youth Open Source Forum. Their projects ranged from endangered-language preservation and AI collaboration in Minecraft to community maps and language research databases.

The Women in Open Source Forum, a COSCon program since the first conference, focused on helping more women take visible roles in engineering, operations, and community contribution. The Open Source Talent Development Forum connected foundation strategy, university education, project experience, career development, and sustainable community growth.

## Open Source for Knowledge and the Public Good

A special reading session marked the second edition of *Open Source Law, Policy and Practice*. Translators and community experts discussed open source economics, motivation, legal practice, and current challenges.

The OpenGood Forum presented projects in rural governance, accessible technology, shared language data, disability support, and rare-disease communities. A roundtable examined how open source public-interest projects can become sustainable.

## A Global and Sustainable Ecosystem

The Global Open Source Development Forum brought together researchers, companies, legal experts, and community leaders to discuss international cooperation, Chinese practice, and changing technology. A separate forum on global open source business explored economics, governance, international growth, and sustainable business models.

## Open Source Night and Community Awards

At Open Source Night, KaiYuanShe board members looked back on ten years of COSCon with volunteers, organizers, speakers, and partners. The community recognized contributors in four groups:

- **Open Source Stars:** Cui Chenyang and Hui Shiji
- **Community Partnership Stars:** Mario Behling for FOSSASIA, Nick Vidal for OSI, and Meng Yingxia for CSDN
- **COSCon Stars:** Chao Qian and Tang Xiaoyin
- **Outstanding Volunteers:** Ding Wenhao, Ding Xin, Liu Tiandong, Liu Zhijie, Liao Jingyi, Li Jiaxin, Li Siying, Li Nan, Duan Yanxing, Wang Yongjie, Zang Peng, and Zhao Wenhan

COSCon'25 showed how open source grows through technical depth, open discussion, patient community work, and people who choose to contribute. KaiYuanShe thanks every volunteer whose careful preparation and support made the event possible.

Conference videos and approved presentation materials will be released through KaiYuanShe's official channels.
articles.author: COSCon'25

articles.title: Join Us: KaiYuanShe's 2026 Volunteer Recruitment Is Open
articles.description: KaiYuanShe is recruiting volunteers for city communities, media and design, global outreach, community partnerships, and finance.
articles.content:
# About KaiYuanShe

Founded in 2014, KaiYuanShe is a vendor-neutral, volunteer-led, non-profit open source community. We work by the principles of contribution, consensus, and co-governance. Our mission covers open source governance, global collaboration, community development, and project incubation.

## What We Ask of Volunteers

Volunteers should support KaiYuanShe's principles and mission, understand the [KaiYuanShe Charter](https://kaiyuanshe.cn/charter), and follow the [Code of Conduct](https://kaiyuanshe.cn/governance/code-of-conduct).

## What Volunteers Receive

Volunteers can join many KaiYuanShe events for free or at a reduced price, meet experienced open source contributors, and learn through real community work. Outstanding long-term volunteers may be nominated for formal membership. We can also provide recommendation letters for strong contributors and relevant internship certificates for student volunteers who have contributed for at least three months.

## Open Roles

### KCC City Community Operations

Help organize KaiYuanShe City Community activities. If your city does not yet have a KCC, you may apply to start one with two other local organizers.

### Media and Brand Team

We are looking for designers and social media volunteers. Work includes planning content for WeChat, video channels, Xiaohongshu, and other platforms, as well as designing event posters and community merchandise.

You should have an interest in open source, clear communication skills, and a good visual sense. Experience with tools such as Photoshop, Illustrator, Figma, Xiumi, or other publishing and design tools is useful.

### Global Social Media Operator

Help KaiYuanShe connect with the global open source community through X, LinkedIn, Facebook, and other international platforms. You will plan English content, tell stories about Chinese contributors and projects, follow global open source trends, and join conversations with communities around the world.

Good English writing and communication skills are important. We also value curiosity, knowledge of online culture, and an active interest in software and technical communities.

### Community Partnership Team

Support relationships with open source communities, foundations, companies, and universities. Work includes event planning, partner communication, documentation, livestreams, and joint promotion. Volunteers should be able to contribute about three to five hours each week.

### Finance Team

Help organize accounts and prepare quarterly and annual reports. This role suits careful, responsible volunteers who are comfortable with spreadsheets.

## Apply

Use the form below. You can also list another team that interests you.

https://kaiyuanshe.feishu.cn/share/base/form/shrcntepbkm5aYu8wnhhXRgej0b

# Introduction

KaiYuanShe was founded in October 2014 as a volunteer-led, non-profit open source community. Our work focuses on open source governance, global collaboration, community development, and open source projects.

2020 was a difficult year. We introduced the theme **Open Source for Good** and worked with many communities to respond to the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic. We also published the Open Source Manifesto and continued building KaiYuanShe as a welcoming home for open source contributors.

This annual report reviews our events, research, working groups, projects, and finances during 2020.

## About KaiYuanShe

KaiYuanShe is a vendor-neutral, volunteer-led, non-profit alliance of communities, individuals, and companies that support open source. We follow the principles of contribution, consensus, and co-governance. Our goal is to help build a healthy, sustainable ecosystem and connect China's open source community with the world.

articles.title: KaiYuanShe Advisory Committee Visits SenseTime to Discuss the Open AI Ecosystem
articles.description: On October 17, 2025, more than 20 members of the KaiYuanShe Board and Advisory Committee visited SenseTime in Beijing for an in-depth exchange on open source AI and real-world adoption.
articles.content:
![KaiYuanShe at SenseTime](https://res.cloudinary.com/drqfxt4jl/image/upload/v1764078149/kyswebsite/ps5jl0v0uqbi0x4ymcwc.webp)

On October 17, 2025, more than 20 members of the KaiYuanShe Board and Advisory Committee visited SenseTime in Beijing. The group discussed how open source can support AI innovation, stronger developer ecosystems, and practical adoption across industries.

SenseTime representatives introduced the company's integrated approach to large models, AI infrastructure, and applications. The visitors also saw examples from smart cities, finance, office tools, and internet services.

## SenseTime's Open Source Work

Wang Zhihong, R&D Director of SenseTime's AI infrastructure business, presented the company's work in model training, inference optimization, and developer tooling. He highlighted **LazyLLM**, a low-code framework for building multi-agent applications with large language models.

SenseTime described four goals for its open source work:

- make research easier to reproduce and extend;
- build open standards and a trusted ecosystem;
- improve collaboration across software and hardware; and
- lower the barrier to using AI in real products.

## A Global View of Open Source

KaiYuanShe co-founder and board member Chen Yang shared lessons from the Open Source Congress 2025 in Brussels. Participants there were interested in the rapid growth of China's community-led open source work and in China's approach to policy and compliance. European open source leaders also discussed growing regulatory pressure and the difficulty of communication among policymakers, companies, and communities.

KaiYuanShe Chair Jiang Bo then presented a landscape report on the open source large-model ecosystem. The report covers 114 widely followed projects across AI infrastructure and AI agents, with additional insight into AI coding, model serving, developer profiles, and changing technology trends.

## Practical Advice from the Experts

- **Wang Zhihong:** A strong open source project must first be useful and easy to use. It should follow common sense and give developers a clear experience.
- **Zhuang Biaowei:** A community can multiply the impact of an internal development team by enabling many more contributors to work together.
- **Professor Wang Wei:** Great projects design the entire developer journey, including documentation, testing, sandboxes, governance, and feedback.
- **Zhang Wensong:** Do one important thing exceptionally well, because users ultimately pay for results.

The visit brought together practical AI work and community experience. KaiYuanShe will continue working with companies, universities, foundations, and open source communities to support a healthy and sustainable AI ecosystem.

## About the Advisory Committee

Founded in 2018, the KaiYuanShe Advisory Committee includes experienced leaders from global foundations, major open source projects, investment organizations, universities, research institutions, technology media, and company open source offices.

Organizations interested in hosting a future exchange can contact `emily@kaiyuanshe.org`.

articles.title: Share Your Open Source Story: KaiYuanShe Welcomes Submissions
articles.description: KaiYuanShe's official WeChat channel is now open for ongoing submissions. We welcome practical stories, lessons, and ideas from across the open source community.
articles.content:
# Share Your Open Source Story

Every open source project is shaped by more than code. The lessons behind a release, the people who keep a community moving, and the ideas that change how we work are all worth sharing.

KaiYuanShe's official WeChat channel welcomes ongoing submissions from open source contributors, maintainers, community organizers, researchers, and users.

## What We Are Looking For

Our editorial focus follows KaiYuanShe's four core areas.

### Open Source Governance

We welcome practical writing about project and foundation governance, community decision-making, contribution processes, licensing, patents, compliance, and lessons from teams of any size.

### Global Collaboration

Tell us about international conferences, cross-border projects, cultural differences in collaboration, useful practices from global communities, or the opportunities and challenges Chinese open source projects face when working internationally.

### Community Development

Share how you started or grew a community, supported contributors, organized events, handled disagreements, built an inclusive culture, or learned from an experiment that did not go as planned.

### Project Incubation

We are interested in the full life of an open source project: validating an idea, releasing a first version, finding early users, growing a contributor base, improving sustainability, and balancing public value with business needs.

We also welcome thoughtful reading notes, industry observations, and honest reviews of lessons learned.

> We are not accepting promotional submissions for events or products through this channel. For partnership requests, contact the Community Partnership Team: slibre@kaiyuanshe.org.

## Editorial Guidelines

Submissions should:

1. offer a clear, informed point of view;
2. be concise, engaging, and easy to read; and
3. help readers understand or practice open source more effectively.

## How to Submit

Use the submission form below:

https://kaiyuanshe.feishu.cn/share/base/form/shrcnrucVx99Xw2fjlWqoTwuEOc

![Submission QR code](https://res.cloudinary.com/drqfxt4jl/image/upload/v1764044743/kyswebsite/zwxyueeuh0sbyh2uiph9.webp)

We will contact you within one week, whether or not the article is selected. Authors of accepted original articles will also receive a small KaiYuanShe community gift.

The Media and Brand Team is also looking for volunteers in writing, graphic design, and social media. To join, email jiangbo@kaiyuanshe.org or add WeChat contact `nadia61`.
